forces.title: Proliferating AI and sophisticated cyber-attacks increase GCC strategic importance.
forces.description: The global landscape is marked by complex geopolitical and economic uncertainty, AI adoption, and intense cyber-warfare. This leads to sophisticated cyberattacks, heightened regulatory scrutiny, and novel risks from AI and OT. These challenges have positioned Cyber GCCs as strategic pillars for resilience, innovation, and leadership in digital risk management for their global organizations.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: GCCs' growing IP concentration elevates cyber resilience importance.
forces.description: The increasing concentration of intellectual property, sensitive data, digital assets, AI-driven systems, and globally interconnected operations within GCCs has made cyber resilience a boardroom priority. The sustained success of the GCC ecosystem is now increasingly dependent on organizations' ability to establish trust, secure digital operations, and maintain confidence among all stakeholders, requiring advanced security strategies.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Evolving threat landscape demands advanced, resilience-focused cybersecurity for GCCs.
forces.description: The cybersecurity landscape is rapidly evolving due to the convergence of cloud computing, artificial intelligence, software-defined infrastructure, operational technology, and increasingly sophisticated threat actors. This complex environment necessitates that organizations, particularly GCCs, move beyond traditional security models to embrace resilience-focused approaches that prioritize preparedness, adaptability, and continuous risk management, driving investment in advanced threat detection and AI-enabled security.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Global cybersecurity talent shortage drives reliance on GCCs.
forces.description: Amidst geopolitical conflicts and rapid AI/cloud adoption, the world faces a growing shortage of cybersecurity talent, especially specialized skills. This talent gap forces global organizations to rethink cybersecurity expertise scaling, increasingly turning to distributed and global teams, including India's GCCs, which are seen as providing more reliable outcomes in this challenging environment.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: AI-driven cyberattacks amplify risks, increasing demand for GCC cybersecurity.
forces.description: Cybercriminals are leveraging AI to create more sophisticated phishing campaigns and identity-driven attacks, posing a significant "double challenge" for organizations. They must manage external AI-introduced risks while also ensuring their internal AI tools are safe, transparent, and well-governed. This heightens the need for specialized cybersecurity expertise, making GCCs a crucial resource for global organizations in addressing these advanced threats.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Global imperatives of Trust, Talent, Transformation drive Cyber GCC investments.
forces.description: As AI redefines business and cybersecurity, global conversation centers on "Trust, Talent, and Transformation." Organizations that invest in strong digital foundations, cyber resilience, future-ready cybersecurity talent, and globally coordinated risk management will be best positioned. Thousands of organizations are already investing in India-based Cyber GCCs, realizing significant strategic and business benefits, highlighting India's talent, innovation, and scale.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: India's expanding cyber GCC workforce, a significant global resource.
forces.description: The cyber GCC workforce in India is growing significantly. Over 25% of cyber GCCs now house nearly 50% of their global cybersecurity workforce in India, and 22% operate large cyber teams exceeding 100 professionals. This trend underscores India's deep talent pool and its increasing role as a strategic hub for global cybersecurity operations, reflecting a major driver for the GCC model.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs' influence grows with global reporting and committee presence.
forces.description: The role and influence of cyber GCCs are expanding significantly. A majority (51%) of organizations now have team members outside India reporting directly to India-based GCC cyber leadership. Furthermore, 80% of cyber GCCs maintain a leadership presence in global cybersecurity committees, indicating a clear shift towards greater strategic responsibility and integration within the parent company's global cybersecurity framework.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Skilled cybersecurity resources and innovation drive GCC model adoption.
forces.description: The primary drivers for leveraging the GCC model are the availability of skilled cybersecurity resources, uninterrupted service delivery, and continuous innovation and agility. These factors highlight India's strength as a talent hub and its capability to provide advanced, resilient cybersecurity operations, making GCCs a preferred choice for global organizations seeking strategic value and operational excellence in digital risk management.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Expanding scope, IT collaboration, and budget constraints fuel GCC growth.
forces.description: Cyber GCC growth is significantly influenced by several key factors. These include the expansion of cybersecurity functions being delivered by GCCs, seamless collaboration with internal IT and other functions within the parent organization, and cost efficiencies driven by budget constraints in global locations. These elements underscore the increasing strategic importance and operational value that GCCs provide to multinational corporations.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs increasingly collaborate with external innovation ecosystems.
forces.description: A significant 69% of cyber GCCs in India are actively engaging with a broader external ecosystem, including start-ups, academia, government bodies, PSUs, law enforcement, think tanks, and industry associations. This strategic collaboration enables GCCs to tap into external agility, research depth, and regulatory guidance, fostering more adaptive and resilient cybersecurity functions and driving innovation within the sector.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: AI security emerges as key function for cyber GCCs.
forces.description: AI security is rapidly emerging as a critical cybersecurity function, with cyber GCCs increasingly delivering these services. This new focus complements existing core functions such as cybersecurity risk assessments, cybersecurity operations, Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), and Identity and Access Management (IAM), indicating an expansion of GCC capabilities into advanced, AI-specific security domains.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Evolving regulatory and emerging tech risks challenge Cyber GCCs.
forces.description: Cyber GCC leadership faces significant cybersecurity challenges, including navigating a changing regulatory landscape (13%), managing third-party cybersecurity risk (11%), and addressing the rise in attacks driven by emerging technologies (9%). Challenges in AI security, OT security, cloud security, and software supply chain security are rapidly evolving, demanding continuous adaptation and strategic responses from GCCs to maintain resilience.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Global boards prioritize AI misuse, OT, supply chain security risks for GCCs.
forces.description: Global boards are increasingly tracking top cybersecurity risks, including AI misuse, OT security risk, software supply chain security risk, third-party security risk, critical infrastructure risk, cloud expansion risk, and regulatory risk. This prioritization directly shapes the strategic mandates and operational responsibilities of Cyber GCCs, requiring them to develop and implement advanced solutions to address these high-level, complex threats for their parent organizations.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs enhance capabilities with fusion centers and COEs.
forces.description: Cyber GCCs have significantly scaled up their capabilities by establishing cyber fusion centers and dedicated cybersecurity Centers of Excellence (COEs), alongside maturing and expanding Security Operations Centers (SOCs). Key benefits realized include faster incident response times (21%), improved threat intelligence sharing (21%), and better overall cybersecurity outcomes (21%), demonstrating a strategic investment in advanced security infrastructure and expertise.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Financial services GCC leads global cybersecurity audits, including AI governance.
forces.description: A leading financial services GCC has established a robust technology audit program, delivering global risk-based cybersecurity internal audits. This includes integrated assurance over technology environments supporting critical functions like payments, asset/wealth management, and global markets. The audit scope now specifically covers cyber resilience, cloud security, privileged access, security operations, and importantly, AI governance and end-to-end AI/ML lifecycle controls, strengthening oversight of emerging AI risks.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs leverage global privacy expertise for DPDPA compliance.
forces.description: With the introduction of the Data Protection and Privacy Act (DPDPA), cyber GCCs in India are playing a crucial role in helping their global organizations achieve compliance. They are leveraging their extensive global privacy experience and expertise to manage compliance activities, including data mapping, consent management, data breach response, and privacy by design, thereby enhancing their strategic value in navigating complex regulatory landscapes.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Gen AI/AI-powered training popular for Cyber GCC talent upskilling.
forces.description: Cyber GCCs are increasingly adopting advanced methods for talent development. Gen AI/AI-powered training and awareness programs, active participation in industry forums, collaborative learning sessions, and knowledge base portals are the most popular means to upskill and cross-skill cybersecurity teams in 2026. This reflects a strategic investment in emerging technologies to enhance the capabilities and future-readiness of the GCC workforce.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCC annual attrition rate declines significantly.
forces.description: Cyber Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India have experienced a significant reduction in their annual attrition rates. Approximately 57% of cyber GCCs registered an attrition rate of 7% or less, a notable improvement that suggests increased stability and retention within their cybersecurity talent pools. This lower attrition indicates a more mature and attractive employment environment for cybersecurity professionals.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Compensation, market demand, location challenge Cyber GCC talent.
forces.description: Cyber GCCs continue to face multifaceted challenges in attracting and retaining top cybersecurity talent. The primary issues identified are competitive compensation and rewards, high market demand for similar specialized skills, and location preferences of candidates. These factors necessitate strategic and tailored approaches from GCCs to build and sustain a robust cybersecurity workforce at scale in India.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs nurturing fresh talent with structured multi-layered approach.
forces.description: To build a sustainable cybersecurity talent pipeline, cyber GCCs are adopting a structured and multi-layered approach for onboarding and integrating fresh talent. This includes early exposure, formal training, continuous skill development, and providing practical experience. This strategy aims to effectively transition freshers into complex cybersecurity roles, reflecting the growing need to scale expertise and address talent shortages.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: AI-powered learning boosts risk culture in Cyber GCCs.
forces.description: Cyber GCCs are increasingly adopting AI-powered cybersecurity learning and assistance as a key initiative to embed and sustain a robust risk culture, emulating global organizations' defense-in-depth approach. This demonstrates a proactive embrace of emerging technologies not just for operational security, but also for enhancing organizational awareness and preparedness against evolving cyber threats, transforming cybersecurity education.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: AI adoption introduces new attack surfaces, making AI security existential.
forces.description: The widespread adoption of AI across business and enterprise functions, facilitated by GCCs, introduces significant new attack surfaces. These include AI model-powered adversarial threats, shadow AI, third-party AI risk, and AI regulatory compliance challenges. Recent AI models have elevated cybersecurity as a top risk for governments, businesses, and consumers, transforming AI security into an existential business issue that GCCs must address.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Global executive sponsorship boosts AI security functions in GCCs.
forces.description: Global organizations and their cyber GCC leadership are receiving significant sponsorship for AI investments, with high-powered committees and business/technology executives prioritizing AI security and AI for security functions. This executive drive empowers cyber GCCs to be at the forefront of securing AI adoption while simultaneously leveraging AI to enhance cybersecurity effectiveness and efficiency, fostering rapid evolution in these critical areas.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: AI adoption boosts Cyber GCC operational efficiency by 10-40%.
forces.description: AI adoption is proving highly beneficial for cybersecurity and digital risk management within cyber GCCs, leading to significant operational efficiencies. A substantial number of GCCs have reported achieving 10-40% operational efficiencies across various cybersecurity activities by leveraging AI. This includes developing and implementing AI-powered use cases for more effective vulnerability, threat, risk, control, and security awareness management.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Cyber GCCs strategically invest in AI to counter AI-powered threats.
forces.description: In a strategic shift, cyber GCCs are actively tapping into AI quotient, AI skills, and AI investments. This proactive approach aims to leverage artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies to effectively manage and mitigate AI-powered cybersecurity risks and threats. Such investment underscores the GCCs' commitment to staying ahead in a rapidly evolving threat landscape by building internal AI capabilities.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Scaling AI creates intense, fast-paced security challenges for GCCs.
forces.description: As cyber GCCs expand their AI adoption, they are encountering a highly intense and rapidly evolving set of security challenges. These challenges necessitate iterative, continuous, and targeted approaches to risk management. The fast-paced nature of AI development and deployment means GCCs must constantly adapt their security strategies to protect against new vulnerabilities and emerging threats inherent in AI systems.
forces.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

forces.title: Enterprise AI deployment adds cybersecurity and SOC costs.
forces.description: Enterprise-wide AI deployment introduces a broader cost base beyond traditional tech investments, including cloud/GPU infrastructure, model licensing, and significant cybersecurity controls. Security and monitoring costs often appear as SOC overheads, reflecting the increased need for robust security postures to manage AI-related risks. This structural shift in technology investment impacts GCCs by increasing their workload and strategic importance in managing enterprise cybersecurity.
forces.source_title: The new tokenomics of AI: Why CFOs must rethink technology investment models

forces.title: Tech sector's centralized cybersecurity and AI governance impacts GCCs.
forces.description: Technology organizations are exhibiting higher levels of centralization compared to other sectors, particularly in areas like enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, and AI governance. This trend reflects rising risk exposure as technology becomes more embedded in operations. For GCCs, this implies an increased demand to support and integrate with these centralized global functions, potentially broadening their mandate and requiring tighter alignment with parent company governance models.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Cyber and regulatory risks, human oversight critical for AI scaling.
forces.description: Cyber and regulatory risks are top concerns for organizations scaling AI, but the rise of human oversight is equally significant. Organizations realize that successful AI scaling depends on having the right skills, judgment, and governance. This drives demand for GCCs to develop expertise in AI governance, ethical AI, and human-in-the-loop processes, ensuring responsible and secure AI deployment within their global parent companies.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Skills, talent, and cybersecurity resilience are critical tech enablers.
forces.description: Technology leaders identify skills and talent, along with cybersecurity resilience, as the most crucial enablers for tech-strategy success over the coming year. This emphasis highlights the increasing reliance on a skilled workforce and robust security frameworks. For GCCs, this translates into continued demand for their expertise in talent development and cybersecurity operations, solidifying their strategic importance to global tech strategies.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Building future-ready, AI-fluent workforce is key for GCCs.
forces.description: Enterprises are advised to build a future-ready, agent-empowered workforce by redesigning talent strategies focused on upskilling and cultivating AI fluency. This includes developing leaders who can effectively use, manage, and master AI. For GCCs, this signifies a crucial mandate to drive talent transformation and capability building, positioning them as strategic centers for human-AI workforce optimization for their global parent companies.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Technology and Telecommunications

forces.title: Agentic AI drives demand for new deployment-focused talent.
forces.description: The advent of Agentic AI, where AI systems take actions and influence business outcomes, is creating demand for a new generation of deployment-focused talent. Roles like Forward Deployment Engineers, AI orchestrators, and human-in-the-loop supervisors are becoming crucial. For Indian enterprises, and by extension their GCCs, the challenge is to build the capabilities, talent, and operating models required to deploy Agentic AI responsibly and at scale for measurable business impact.
forces.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

forces.title: Ethical concerns, data readiness, skill gaps hinder AI implementation.
forces.description: Indian enterprises face significant barriers to AI implementation, with 62% of CEOs citing ethical concerns, 53% believing their data is not sufficiently AI-ready, and 46% acknowledging technical skill gaps. These challenges are amplified by Agentic AI, which performs actions and influences business outcomes, demanding robust trusted AI governance, enterprise-grade data foundations, and human oversight, representing a key hurdle for GCCs supporting AI deployment.
forces.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook

forces.title: Data privacy, quality, regulation hinder AI scaling, impacting GCCs.
forces.description: Organizations face significant barriers to scaling AI, including data privacy and cybersecurity (42%), data quality (34%), and regulatory uncertainty (31%). These issues stem from deeper enterprise misalignments like fragmented data, inconsistent governance, and uncoordinated workflows. Addressing these constraints is crucial for GCCs, which play a vital role in operationalizing AI at scale for their parent companies, ensuring sustained performance and compliance.
forces.source_title: Global AI Pulse Q2 2026

forces.title: Increased AI investment in infrastructure and security benefits GCCs.
forces.description: Organizations are significantly increasing investments in AI capabilities, with 58% investing in infrastructure, 50% in security, and over 40% in transformation, innovation, and workforce capability. This sustained investment, despite patchy returns, reflects confidence in AI's long-term value. For GCCs, this translates into expanded mandates and opportunities to support parent companies in building AI infrastructure, bolstering security, and developing AI-ready workforces.
forces.source_title: Global AI Pulse Q2 2026

forces.title: India's cost-efficient IT/AI talent pool supports data center growth.
forces.description: India possesses a large and cost-efficient IT and AI talent pool, with software engineer salaries significantly lower than global peers (around USD 20k per annum). This talent pool actively supports data center development and operations, with AI capability expanding rapidly (33% YoY growth in AI hiring) and India contributing nearly 20% of global AI development activities. This talent base acts as a strong draw for global companies, including those establishing or expanding GCCs.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Non-metro cities drive IT hiring, offering ~30% cost savings.
forces.description: Non-metro cities like Udaipur, Vizag, Coimbatore, and Nagpur are driving over 50% of India's IT hiring growth, significantly outpacing traditional hubs like Bengaluru and NCR (12-15%) in H1 2025. This structural shift towards tier-II and tier-III hubs attracts demand in AI, cloud, and cybersecurity, offering approximately 30% cost savings. This trend influences GCC location strategies, promoting diversification and access to a wider talent pool.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Google's $15bn AI Hub investment boosts India's AI ecosystem for GCCs.
forces.description: Google's commitment of US$15 billion over 2026-2030 for an AI Hub and data center in Visakhapatnam represents its largest investment in India to advance AI capabilities and services. While primarily focused on AI infrastructure (data centers are SE11), the establishment of a major AI hub significantly enhances India's AI ecosystem and talent pool, providing a substantial tailwind for GCCs seeking to leverage advanced AI skills and resources for their global operations.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Strong IT hiring and innovation centers drive GCC talent demand.
forces.description: India's IT hiring is projected to grow by 7% in FY27, fueled by the expansion of innovation centers by global technology companies, a robust domestic talent pool specializing in next-generation technologies, and government-led digitalization initiatives. This trend directly benefits Global Capability Centers (GCCs) as they are prime beneficiaries of this talent surge and often represent the innovation centers established by multinational corporations in India.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Tax holiday for cloud services boosts India's tech ecosystem for GCCs.
forces.description: The 2026-27 Budget proposes a tax holiday until 2047 for foreign companies providing cloud services to global customers through data centers in India. While directly impacting cloud and data center infrastructure (SE11), this policy significantly enhances India's attractiveness as a hub for technology operations. This provides an indirect tailwind for GCCs by reducing operational costs and improving the overall investment climate for technology services they deliver.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: PLI scheme strengthens IT Hardware manufacturing, benefiting GCC product engineering.
forces.description: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for IT Hardware and its upgraded version have successfully generated significant production (INR 10,014 crore), investment (INR 522 crore), and created 3,879 jobs as of December 2024. This growth in domestic tech manufacturing strengthens the overall electronics ecosystem. For GCCs, particularly those involved in product engineering and hardware-related R&D, this creates opportunities for local sourcing, collaboration, and talent, fostering greater domestic integration.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Emerging technologies drive strong job growth in India's IT ecosystem.
forces.description: India's IT ecosystem is poised for robust growth, with emerging technologies projected to drive a 20% increase in new jobs in 2025, building on a 17% increase in 2024. This signifies a buoyant job market fueled by advancements in areas like AI and other next-generation technologies. This trend provides a strong talent pipeline and growth opportunities for Global Capability Centers (GCCs) operating in India, expanding their workforce and capabilities.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Tata's $11bn Innovation City boosts India's AI/semiconductor for GCCs.
forces.description: Tata Group's plan to invest US$11 billion in an Innovation City near Navi Mumbai International Airport aims to bolster India's position in AI and semiconductor services. This massive investment will create a vibrant ecosystem that attracts talent, fosters R&D, and develops advanced infrastructure. Such developments provide a significant tailwind for GCCs by enhancing the overall talent pool and creating a more sophisticated environment for tech and product engineering operations.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Adani's $100bn AI data center investment strengthens India's AI infrastructure.
forces.description: Adani's plan to invest US$100 billion in AI data centers over the next decade, integrating AI infrastructure with renewable energy, will significantly enhance India's digital capabilities. While primarily focused on physical data centers (SE11), this massive investment will create a robust foundation for AI-driven operations. This provides a strong tailwind for GCCs by improving access to high-performance AI compute and advanced infrastructure for their tech, analytics, and AI/ML functions.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Semiconductor manufacturing boosts India's tech ecosystem for GCCs.
forces.description: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Limited is establishing a semiconductor manufacturing facility in Gujarat, backed by a significant investment (INR 7,584 crore) and supported by India’s Design Linked Incentive scheme. This initiative, a joint venture with Renesas Electronics America Inc. and STARS Microelectronic, strengthens India's semiconductor ecosystem. For GCCs involved in product engineering, hardware design, or embedded systems, this provides a burgeoning local supply chain and specialized talent pool to collaborate with.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: IndiaAI Mission fosters national AI ecosystem for GCCs.
forces.description: The Government of India's launch of the IndiaAI Mission with a substantial outlay of INR 10,372 crore (US$1.25 billion) aims to foster the development of the nation's overall AI ecosystem. This initiative provides a significant tailwind for Global Capability Centers (GCCs) by enhancing the availability of AI talent, promoting R&D, and creating a more robust environment for AI/ML and product engineering activities, accelerating innovation and capability building.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Liberalized space FDI signals broader tech investment drive.
forces.description: India has liberalized its Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) regulations for the space sector, allowing up to 100% FDI in satellite manufacturing and components, with increased limits for launch vehicles and satellite operations. This aims to attract global capital and advanced technology. While specific to space, this policy change signals a broader government commitment to fostering high-tech industries and global investment, creating a more favorable environment for GCCs in advanced engineering and technology domains.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: India's surging AI patent filings indicate strong R&D.
forces.description: Between 2010 and 2025, India filed over 86,000 AI patents, representing 25% of all tech patents. Notably, filings from 2021-25 were seven times higher than 2010-15, with 63% originating domestically. This surge in AI-related intellectual property signifies India's burgeoning R&D capabilities and innovation ecosystem, providing a strong tailwind for GCCs seeking to engage in advanced AI/ML and product engineering for their parent companies.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Software services exports driven by AI, strong talent, and GCCs.
forces.description: India's software services exports are projected to grow at a 5.80% CAGR from US$147 billion in 2025 to US$206.15 billion by 2031. This growth is significantly driven by value-led partnerships, the availability of strong IT talent, increasing AI adoption, and the expanding role of Global Capability Centers (GCCs). The mention of GCCs as a key driver underscores their integral contribution to India's overall IT export success and increasing global relevance.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: India AI Mission funding boost supports GCC AI capabilities.
forces.description: The India AI Mission has received a significant budget increase, allocated INR 2,000 crore (US$236.4 million) in 2025-26, up from INR 173 crore (US$8.6 million) in 2024-25. This substantial increase in funding for AI initiatives strengthens the national AI ecosystem. This provides a strong tailwind for GCCs by enhancing research, development, and talent availability in AI, directly supporting their AI/ML and product engineering functions for global parent companies.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: India's R&D incentives position it as global powerhouse, aiding GCCs.
forces.description: India is aggressively expanding R&D tax incentives, customs benefits, and funding, including a proposed INR 1 trillion (US$11.30 billion) innovation fund, to become a global R&D powerhouse. This strategic focus targets emerging areas like AI, green technologies, biotech, and semiconductors. Such robust policy support creates a highly favorable environment for GCCs to expand their research, product engineering, and innovation mandates for their global parent companies in India.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Databricks' $250mn investment boosts India's data/AI R&D.
forces.description: Databricks plans a strategic investment exceeding US$250 million in India over three years (by 2028) to significantly boost innovation, training, and R&D in data and artificial intelligence. This investment will enhance India's capabilities and talent pool in critical data and AI domains. For GCCs, this provides an enriched ecosystem, access to advanced tools and training, and a stronger talent pipeline to support their data analytics, AI/ML, and product engineering functions.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: India's GCC leadership projected to employ 3.3 million by 2030.
forces.description: India has solidified its position as the leading Global Capability Centre (GCC) destination, with projections indicating the sector will employ 3.3 million professionals by 2030. This growth is underpinned by India's skilled workforce and supportive policy environment. The expansion underscores the increasing confidence of multinational corporations in India's capabilities for high-value tech, analytics, AI/ML, and product engineering functions.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Engineering R&D market growth boosts GCC product engineering.
forces.description: India's engineering R&D and product development market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 12%, reaching US$63 billion by 2025 from US$31 billion in 2019. This significant expansion is driven by companies offshoring complete product responsibility to India. For GCCs, this represents a major tailwind, enhancing their role in product engineering, design, and development for their global parent companies, capitalizing on India's talent and cost efficiencies.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: India's vast developer talent pool strengthens outsourcing and GCCs.
forces.description: India commands approximately 17.58% of the global software outsourcing market, supported by the world's largest developer workforce of over 5.4 million software engineers. The country's universities further bolster this advantage by producing more than 500,000 new graduates annually. This immense and continuously replenished talent pool is a critical tailwind for Global Capability Centers (GCCs), ensuring a consistent influx of skilled professionals for their tech, analytics, AI/ML, and product engineering operations.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Most companies use GCCs for engineering R&D, India a top destination.
forces.description: A significant 85% of surveyed companies leverage Global Capability Centers (GCCs) for their engineering R&D activities, highlighting the strategic importance of these captive centers. India stands out as a top destination for outsourced innovation services, including engineering R&D, with nearly half of companies also utilizing Engineering Service Providers. This trend solidifies GCCs' role in advanced product development and innovation for global corporations.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

forces.title: Increased BFSI spending and GenAI drive IT services growth, benefiting GCCs.
forces.description: The IT services sector is projected to experience steady revenue growth of 7-9% in FY26, significantly driven by increased spending from the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector and the rapid adoption of generative AI initiatives. This robust demand from BFSI, coupled with advancements in AI, acts as a strong tailwind for Global Capability Centers (GCCs), expanding their opportunities in tech, analytics, AI/ML, and product engineering services for financial institutions.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Disruptive technologies create new growth avenues for GCCs.
forces.description: Disruptive technologies such as cloud computing, social media, data analytics, artificial intelligence, machine learning, blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), and robotic process automation are creating significant new growth avenues for IT companies. For Global Capability Centers (GCCs), these technologies represent core areas for innovation, capability development, and service expansion, driving demand for their expertise in tech, analytics, AI/ML, and product engineering functions for global parent companies.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Experian's GIC expansion in Hyderabad boosts emerging tech talent.
forces.description: Experian is significantly expanding its global innovation center (GIC) in Hyderabad, aiming to reach 4,000 employees over the next three to five years. This expansion is strategically focused on developing and leveraging emerging technologies within the BFSI sector, including cloud computing, big data analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning. This initiative directly contributes to the growth of specialized tech talent and advanced capabilities within India's GCC ecosystem.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Rapid public cloud market growth boosts GCC cloud services.
forces.description: India's public cloud services market is experiencing rapid growth, reaching US$10.9 billion in 2024 and projected to hit US$30.4 billion by 2029 at a CAGR of 22.6%. This accelerated adoption of cloud computing provides a significant tailwind for Global Capability Centers (GCCs) by driving demand for cloud migration, managed services, and cloud-native application development, expanding their scope and strategic relevance in global cloud strategies.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: AI-driven productivity shifts contracts to outcome-based models.
forces.description: AI-driven productivity gains, estimated at 20-40%, are fundamentally shifting client expectations from traditional "per-FTE" contracts to outcome-based models. This structural change demands pay-for-results, fixed-price, subscription, and usage-based deals. For Global Capability Centers (GCCs), this necessitates adapting their service delivery and pricing strategies, focusing on value creation and efficiency, pushing them towards higher-value, more integrated solutions, exemplified by companies adopting AI-platform contracts.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: M&A surge for niche skills benefits GCCs' specialized capabilities.
forces.description: Deal-making in the tech sector is surging, with firms actively acquiring companies to gain niche skills, such as Infosys acquiring cybersecurity firm The Missing Link and semiconductor design firm InSemi. This trend highlights the high demand for specialized capabilities in cloud, AI, cyber, and chip design. For GCCs, this signals the critical importance of developing and offering these advanced, in-demand skills, positioning them as strategic assets for parent companies through capability expansion and M&A integration.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Tech Mahindra's AI COE fosters language model development, aids GCCs.
forces.description: Tech Mahindra established an NVIDIA-powered AI Centre of Excellence in October 2024 to develop Hindi/domain-specific large language models (Project Indus 2.0). While Tech Mahindra is an IT services provider (IN080101), this initiative strengthens the broader AI ecosystem in India. This development benefits GCCs by enhancing the availability of specialized AI tools, fostering expertise in localized AI/ML, and providing a benchmark for product engineering in advanced language model applications for their parent companies.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: RDI Scheme boosts private R&D and tech self-reliance.
forces.description: The Department of Science and Technology's RDI Scheme, launched with INR 1,00,000 crore (US$11.62 billion), aims to significantly enhance private-sector R&D and India’s technological self-reliance. This initiative supports strategic technologies through long-term financing via the ANRF and designated Second-Level Fund Managers. For GCCs, this creates a robust ecosystem for advanced research and product engineering, encouraging them to expand their high-value R&D mandates for global parent companies in India.
forces.source_title: Science And Technology Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Cyber GCCs are strategic pillars for resilience and innovation.
viewpoints.description: KPMG's Head of Cyber Security & Technology in India notes that Cyber GCCs in India have evolved beyond augmenting global teams. They now lead, innovate, and strategize cybersecurity and digital risk management, enabling parent organizations to realize significant value and business growth amidst geopolitical and economic uncertainty, supply chain disruption, and increasing AI adoption and cyber warfare.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: GCCs evolve to strategic ecosystems driving innovation and competitive advantage.
viewpoints.description: The CEO of DSCI notes that Global Capability Centers have transformed from efficiency-focused models into strategic ecosystems. They now drive innovation, digital engineering, artificial intelligence, advanced analytics, and cybersecurity at scale, becoming critical contributors to the competitive advantage of global enterprises. Cybersecurity maturity is a key differentiator, with GCCs expected to lead digital transformation security.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: India's GCC ecosystem central to global innovation and R&D.
viewpoints.description: In 2026, India's Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are poised to create strategic value for global organizations, being at the heart of business transformation. Organizations worldwide increasingly look to India to accelerate innovation, research and development, and business operations, delivering at speed, scale, quality, and commercial efficiency, while also advancing critical business objectives.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: India's cybersecurity workforce and ecosystem empower GCCs with competitive advantage.
viewpoints.description: The Director General of CERT-In notes that India has successfully built a world-class cybersecurity workforce and a sustainable ecosystem, fostering innovation and indigenous capabilities. Cyber GCCs have become an inherent and strategic component, offering global organizations competitive advantage in resilience, innovation, and growth. They play a pivotal role in secure adoption of emerging technologies and delivering measurable business value.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: GCCs are critical for AI adoption, facing new AI security challenges.
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that Global Capability Centres in India are crucial for global organizations adopting AI across business functions. However, AI adoption introduces significant new attack surfaces, including adversarial threats, shadow AI, third-party AI risk, and regulatory compliance challenges, making AI a top and existential cybersecurity risk. Cyber GCCs are at the forefront, both securing AI adoption and leveraging AI to strengthen cybersecurity effectiveness and efficiency.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: Robust AI security is a core differentiator for scaling GCCs.
viewpoints.description: Shalini Pillay, India Leader for Global Capability Centers at KPMG, emphasizes that for GCCs scaling AI adoption, robust AI security is no longer merely a safeguard but has become a core business differentiator. This perspective highlights the critical importance of strong security frameworks and practices in enabling GCCs to achieve competitive advantage in the AI-driven business landscape.
viewpoints.source_title: Secure in India 2026: Cyber GCCs in the age of AI

viewpoints.title: Effective Agentic AI deployment requires new operating models and governance.
viewpoints.description: KPMG emphasizes that success in the Agentic AI era will be determined by effective deployment, not just early adoption. This necessitates a new operating model that combines trusted AI governance, enterprise-grade data foundations, human oversight, and deployment excellence. Indian enterprises, and their GCCs, must move beyond AI experimentation to build organizational capabilities for industrializing AI at scale, which will be the next source of competitive advantage.
viewpoints.source_title: The agentic AI imperative: Why Indian enterprises need a new deployment playbook
